case_name: Carmain et al. v. Charles Schwab & Co., Inc. (Structured Negotiation)
court: No court — resolved through Structured Negotiation (pre-litigation)
docket: N/A — structured negotiation, not filed in court
defendant_revenue_band: >$18B revenue (2024; one of the largest US retail brokerages)
claim_type: ADA Title III — schwab.com, Schwab Mobile, and Thinkorswim web platform inaccessible to blind and visually impaired retail clients; violations of WCAG standards
estimated_costs: No monetary amount disclosed; WCAG 2.2 AA remediation of all Schwab digital properties, quarterly usability testing, third-party vendor compliance requirements

sources.name: Law Office of Lainey Feingold — Charles Schwab 2024 Web and Mobile Accessibility Settlement Agreement (November 2024)

violation_source_evidence: Lainey Feingold settlement summary (lflegal.com/2024/11/schwab-2024-agreement): Specific violations listed in 'Exhibit 1 to the Confidential Addendum' and not publicly disclosed. However, the settlement explicitly required: (1) WCAG 2.2 AA remediation for schwab.com, Schwab Mobile, and Thinkorswim — implying broad non-conformance; (2) 'No inaccessible CAPTCHA' commitment — directly indicating CAPTCHAs lacked accessible alternatives; (3) Critical conformance issues on 'top 10 experiences' remediated by September 30, 2024 — implying core user flows were inaccessible to blind clients using screen readers. Claimants were four blind Schwab retail clients who could not independently access brokerage services.
summary_one_line: Four blind Charles Schwab clients secured a 2024 structured negotiation agreement requiring Schwab to achieve WCAG 2.2 AA compliance across schwab.com, Schwab Mobile, and Thinkorswim — with quarterly disability usability testing and vendor compliance obligations.
notes: Effective Date: August 26, 2024. Duration: through October 31, 2026. Claimants: Jon Carmain, Joel Isaac, Kit Lau, Victor Tsaran (four blind Schwab retail clients). Claimants' counsel: Matthew Handley (Handley Farah & Anderson PLLC) and Lainey Feingold (Law Office of Lainey Feingold). Key terms: (1) All new content must conform before release; (2) Critical issues on top 10 experiences remediated by Sept 30, 2024; (3) Mobile app critical issues by Dec 31, 2024; (4) Quarterly usability testing by persons with disabilities; (5) No inaccessible CAPTCHA; (6) Third-party vendors must achieve conformance within 30 days of request. Schwab denied any ADA violations. This is the most recent high-profile financial services accessibility resolution and covers B2B-relevant wealth management platforms. No lawsuit filed — structured negotiation used.
